sections.advice: Dalsnibba junction → Geiranger is 9 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Geiranger → Ornesvingen is 4 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Ornesvingen → Gudbrandsjuvet is 35 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Gudbrandsjuvet → Trollstigen climbs about 858 m in 21 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Trollstigen → Sogge Bridge drops about 858 m over 12 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Geiranger-Trollstigen Norwegian Scenic Route
scenicChapters.narrative: For 2 km this is Geiranger-Trollstigen Norwegian Scenic Route, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Trollstigen
scenicChapters.narrative: A steady rhythm suits this better than bursts. The height arrives whether you hurry or not. The ground tilts up and stays tilted for 31 km. 858 m of it, taken steadily rather than in one wall.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Trollstigen
scenicChapters.narrative: 858 m come off over 18 km at around 7.2%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it — brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

norwegian-scenic-route-geiranger-trollst.story: It goes by way of Dalsnibba junction, Geiranger, Ornesvingen and Gudbrandsjuvet. The highest point is about 1,200 m. Trollstigen is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
